blocks.content: The Constitution has made elaborate provisions to safeguard and ensure the independent and impartial functioning of the judiciary.

rows: Prohibited in all courts in India
Permitted in SC and other HCs where they did not serve

items: Pensions of High Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas their salaries are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Article 50 under the Directive Principles of State Policy mandates the separation of the judiciary from the executive.
The conduct of judges cannot be discussed in Parliament or State Legislatures except during a formal removal motion.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Security of Tenure: Judges can only be removed by the President through a specific constitutional procedure on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Fixed Service Conditions: Salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund and cannot be altered to a judge's disadvantage during their tenure.
Prohibition of Practice: Retired Supreme Court judges are barred from pleading or acting in any court or authority within the territory of India.
Power to Punish for Contempt: Courts possess the inherent power to punish for their contempt to preserve judicial authority and dignity.
Separation from Executive: Article 50 directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
